capabilities.target: customer account records, lookup by email or account id (any customer)

instructions.note: Agent may look up any customer by email or account id, with no restriction to the ticket requester's own account. This is the structural basis for the confused-deputy finding.
The only gate on an irreversible external send is a natural-language rule ('send directly... do not wait unless angry'). There is no structural approval_gate_ref for cap.email_send.
The sole safeguard against disclosing another customer's data to the requester is a single prompt line, with no structural recipient/identity-match validation behind it.

controls.name: Prompt instruction: never share another customer's information
controls.decay_rationale: Enforcement relies entirely on the model choosing to comply with a single prompt line under a persuasive or multi-step injected request. A more capable model is better at rationalizing exceptions ('the customer clearly meant...') and at splitting the disclosure into steps that each look innocuous.

controls.name: Outbound email logging to SIEM
controls.decay_rationale: Logging does not depend on the model and does not decay with capability, but it is purely detective: it records the send after it has already left the boundary, so it does not prevent the irreversible disclosure.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the ticket's system-of-record address
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. If implemented so the send target is taken from the verified ticket record rather than model output, it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Human approval gate (raw action) for email_send on identity mismatch
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. A raw-action approval gate (full recipient and payload visible) would be independent of model capability, unlike a model-summary gate.

controls.name: Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN to the ticket's own customer record
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. A credential scoped per-request to the authenticated ticket's customer id would not decay with model capability, since the model could not read records it has no credential for.

controls.name: Scope MAIL_SVC_TOKEN to the ticket's verified reply address
controls.decay_rationale: Not yet implemented. Restricting the send credential to the verified requester address, resolved from the system of record, would not decay with model capability.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta (TC1): untrusted email drives CRM lookup and unreviewed external send

attack_path.note: Attacker-controlled ticket content enters the agent as untrusted input.
Agent calls get_customer; prompt.md:3 allows lookup by email or account id with no scope restriction.
Agent sends the drafted reply directly for routine tickets with no human approval (prompt.md:5-6), carrying confidential CRM data to an externally reachable address.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version/id change in the platform's model config with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true); monitor model config diffs and upgrade announcements.

evidence.observation: Agent reads untrusted email, looks up the customer, and sends a reply directly for routine tickets with no approval step.
crm_mcp and mail_mcp are reachable with no additional gating described between lookup and send.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN can read every customer record; MAIL_SVC_TOKEN can send to any address; both are broad/shared credentials with no scoping to the requester.

recommendations.action: Bind the reply recipient to the verified email address on the ticket record (system of record), never to a model-chosen or freeform address.
Require raw-action human approval before email_send whenever the retrieved CRM record does not match the ticket requester's verified identity.
Scope CRM_SVC_TOKEN to least privilege, limited to the record tied to the authenticated ticket, removing free-form lookup by email or account id.
Add automated post-send scanning that compares PII in sent emails against the verified requester identity and alerts before any digest window closes.

findings.title: Confused deputy (TC4): broad and shared credentials exceed the requester's authority

attack_path.note: Ticket content requests account information, possibly for an account other than the sender's own, since prompt.md:3 permits lookup by email or account id.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN is broad and can read every customer record; nothing scopes the lookup to the requester's own identity.
MAIL_SVC_TOKEN is a shared service account that can send to any address; the result is returned to the requester regardless of whose record was read.

forecast.watch_signal: Model version/id change in the platform's model config with no separate review (subject.model.swappable=true); monitor model config diffs and upgrade announcements.

evidence.observation: Agent 'may look up any customer by email or account id,' with no check that it matches the requester.
Only a single prompt line ('never share another customer's information') defends against cross-customer disclosure; it is behavioral, not structural.
CRM_SVC_TOKEN reads every record and MAIL_SVC_TOKEN sends to any address; the agent's effective privilege exceeds what an individual customer requester should have.

recommendations.action: Scope MAIL_SVC_TOKEN so it can only send to the email address already associated with the ticket/customer record.
Remove free-form lookup by email or account id; restrict get_customer to the account tied to the authenticated ticket/session.
Alert when a retrieved CRM record's customer id does not match the authenticated requester's identity.

rating.rationale: Both findings start from an untrusted email reaching a confidential CRM read and then an irreversible external send (S3), giving inherent risk of critical under the U x S3 base matrix. The only preventive control in the design is a single behavioral prompt instruction ('never share another customer's information'), which is dependent on model compliance; crediting it at rubric step 4 lowers residual risk to high for both findings, since no structural control (approval gate, recipient confirmation, or scoped credential) exists to sever or narrow the path. SIEM logging is detective only and does not reduce consequence, since disclosure is complete at send time. Runtime notes confirm the model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, so the model_upgrade trigger directly applies to the one dependent control; removing it returns both findings to critical. The control whose decay drives the forecast is ctl.no_share_instruction.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in prompt.md, mcp.json, and the runtime notes; it does not reflect observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest or MCP tools/list response was provided; the exact argument schema for send and get_customer is inferred from the prompt and mcp.json, so capability scope is inferred at medium-to-high confidence rather than directly observed.

No runtime/orchestration config was supplied showing max_unattended_steps or max_runtime_minutes; these are treated as unbounded (null) per the absence of any stated limit, which is a conservative assumption.

The effectiveness of ctl.no_share_instruction is unverified (status: declared, not verified); if red-team testing shows it is reliably bypassed today, true present-day residual risk is closer to critical than high.
